options.text: The process of purifying water by adding chlorine
The process where excess nutrients cause algal blooms, leading to oxygen depletion and death of aquatic life
The natural process of water evaporating from lakes
The process of heavy metals building up in fish

questions.explanation: Eutrophication occurs when excess nutrients (nitrates and phosphates from fertilisers or sewage) enter water, causing rapid algae growth (algal bloom). The algae block light, killing underwater plants. When the algae and plants decompose, bacteria use up dissolved oxygen, suffocating fish and other aquatic life.

questions.stem: Why are heavy metals in water particularly dangerous?

options.text: They make the water taste bad
They are elements that cannot be broken down, bioaccumulate in organisms, and become more concentrated up the food chain
They make the water heavier so fish cannot swim
They cause the water to freeze more easily

questions.explanation: Heavy metals (lead, mercury, cadmium) are elements that cannot be broken down by bacteria. They bioaccumulate in organisms over time and biomagnify up the food chain, meaning top predators have the highest concentrations. Even at low levels, they can cause nervous system damage, cancer, and birth defects.
